title: Admission SLAs and Queue-Ranking Heuristics for Strategic Account Requests
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build a deterministic, transparent system of admission SLAs and queue-ranking heuristics for requests originating from strategic (high-ACV / high-risk) accounts. Goal: reduce time-to-decision for top-account asks, increase predictability for sales/CS, and balance delivery commitments against existing roadmap capacity. Deliverables: (1) scoring function & priority lanes, (2) SLA definitions for intake stages, (3) playbook for cross-functional review and handoffs, (4) dashboard metrics and alerting, (5) rollout plan and pilot with 3 named accounts.
background: Multiple sales and CSM escalations in H2 2025 revealed inconsistent routing and long decision times for feature requests from strategic accounts. Current triage is ad-hoc: PMs bias, engineering capacity surprises, and legal/compliance requirements are frequently surfaced late. We need a repeatable, auditable process so commitments to strategic customers are time-bounded and aligned to measurable risk/impact trade-offs.
proposed_approach: 1) Define an account_score combining ARR, strategic fit, renewal risk, and integration complexity. 2) Create three priority lanes (Rapid Review, Strategic Queue, Normal Roadmap) with clear SLAs per stage (intake acknowledged, initial evaluation, decision/commit). 3) Implement a risk-adjusted scheduling multiplier so infrastructure/infra-heavy requests reduce expected delivery windows. 4) Require a minimum acceptance checklist (security/legal, data residency, SSO) before SLA countdown proceeds. 5) Expose queue and SLA status in Console for internal stakeholders and CS teams.
priority_lanes: Rapid Review: immediate exec+PM evaluation, SLA: acknowledge <= 4h, evaluation <= 3 business days, decision or programmatic alternative
Strategic Queue: scheduled scoping and triage, SLA: acknowledge <= 24h, evaluation <= 10 business days, decision documented and queued for next roadmap cycle
Normal Roadmap: standard backlog intake with credit scoring, SLA: acknowledge <= 5 business days, scope during next planning cycle
scoring_components: Strategic Fit (0-30): product alignment, referenceability, partner value
Renewal Risk (0-20): contract health, upcoming renewal date, NPS signals
Compliance/Regulatory (0-10): legal blockers that increase cost/time
sla_definitions: Acknowledge: system-generated receipt + CS nudge to PM within SLA window
Initial Evaluation: PM + Eng + Solutions meeting to slot request and surface blockers
Decision/Commit: documented commitment (timeline, scope caveats, owner) or formal decline with rationale
acceptance_criteria: Scoring function implemented in Intake form and validated on historical backlog
Priority lanes created in Linear with automation that assigns lane based on score + manual override logging
SLA timers visible in Console and CS dashboard (time-to-ack, time-to-decision)
Pilot run completed with 3 strategic accounts and post-pilot retrospective documented
metrics_to_track: % of strategic requests that result in roadmap commitment within 1 cycle
Forecast accuracy vs actual delivery date for committed items
tradeoffs_and_risks: Prioritizing top accounts may reduce throughput for pockets of product-led growth users
Hard SLAs risk overpromising if we do not couple with capacity controls (reserved slots, engineering buffers)
Manual overrides create audit/consistency risk; require mandatory rationale and triage owner
Scoring gamification: sales may attempt to influence inputs — need verifiable signals and approval gates
implementation_steps: Design intake form changes and scoring (PM + Analytics) - owner: Marco
Create Linear workflow + automation rules to auto-assign lanes - owner: Ops Eng
Console dashboard: SLA timers and queue view - owner: Console Eng
Pilot run w/ 3 accounts and structured feedback (CS + Sales) - owner: Solutions Eng
Retrospective and iteration (2-week window after pilot) - owner: Priya
